title: The module $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ of a finite locally free morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a locally free $\mathcal{O}_S$-module of rank $d$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and for every $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] the canonical map $(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)_s\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S,s}}\kappa(s)\to \Gamma(X_s,\mathcal{O}_{X_s})$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the finite-flat pushforward theorem [lem-pc-finite-flat-pushforward-locally-free] to the structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, which is finite locally free over itself. Since finite locally free of degree $d$ means finite, flat and locally finitely presented by [def-pc-finite-locally-free], this gives that $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is finite locally free.

For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ around $s$, finiteness makes $f^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ with $B$ finite over $A$. The affine fibre calculation [lem-pc-finite-affine-fibre-sections], using the affine fibre-product identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], identifies the stalk tensor with $B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$ and the fibre sections with the same algebra. Hence the canonical map in the statement is an isomorphism.

By Step 2, the fibre of the locally free module from Step 1 at $s$ identifies with $\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$. The degree clause in [def-pc-finite-locally-free] says $\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})=d$, so this locally free module has rank $d$ at every point.
